title: One phone number holds the whole thread.
subtitle: The local port agent. Printed in the daily programme every morning, and almost never read.

title: Photograph the port agent's details before you go ashore.
caption: Printed in the daily programme and posted at the gangway. It is the only number that matters if you are watching your ship make way.
brief: Rubber date stamp on its pad beside a folded printed sheet, harsh window light, damp-curled edges. Nothing legible.
source: Jordan's own stamp and paper; else Unsplash 'rubber stamp ink pad old paper desk'

items.head: Your passport goes to the agent
items.body: Standard protocol. The ship lands the documents of anyone missing with the local port agent before it sails.

items.head: The agent works with the line
items.body: They coordinate with the ship, the local authorities and the line's shore team to rejoin you at the next port.

items.head: Your belongings sail on
items.body: Cabin, luggage and medication continue with the ship. This is why the medication should never have been in the cabin.

items.head: Someone funds the gap
items.body: Who that is was decided the moment you chose between the ship's excursion and a private tour.

left.label: Private tour
items: Coast Guard could not board them

text: Passport, wallet, phone, medication. On your person, always.
sub: Every account of being left behind turns on the same detail: not the lateness, but what the guest happened to be carrying when the gangway went up.

quote: The lateness is rarely the disaster. Being late with nothing in your pockets and no number to call — that is the disaster.

title: Save this. You will want it once.
body: And if you'd like the short version I give clients before a port-heavy sailing, ask me for the port-day note and I'll send it across.
